title: Vending machine brain
prompt:
A snack machine sells one thing for 75 cents. It takes nickels (5), dimes (10), quarters (25), loonies (100) and toonies (200), and hands anything else straight back. Pulling the return lever, input 0, gives back whatever credit is in the machine.

The starter's `main` reads the inputs one at a time, calls `coin(value)` for each, and prints a summary at the end. Write `coin`. The machine's memory, the credit so far and the number of snacks sold, lives in the `.bss` words `credit` and `sold`, not in registers, so it lasts from one call to the next: `coin` loads what it needs, updates it, and stores it back.

Each input prints exactly one line:

- a value it does not take: `rejected v`, and the credit is unchanged
- the return lever: `returned c`, and the credit goes back to 0
- a coin that leaves the credit under 75: `credit c`
- a coin that brings the credit to 75 or more: `vend! change c`, where c is the credit minus 75; the credit goes back to 0 and `sold` goes up by 1

The starter's input prints:

```
credit 25
credit 35
credit 60
credit 70
vend! change 0
sold 1, holding 0
```

`coin` calls `printf`, so it needs a frame, and any of x19 to x28 it uses must be saved and restored.

## what is checked

- the lines above
- the program exits with status 0
- the same checks on other inputs the checker keeps hidden: exactly 75 cents, a toonie, rejected values (a negative one too), the lever on an empty machine, and no input at all
- the state is written back to memory (`str`)
starter:
// a snack machine that sells one item for 75 cents; its memory lives in .bss
define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

define(PRICE, 75)

.data
fmt_in:     .string "%d"
fmt_credit: .string "credit %d\n"
fmt_vend:   .string "vend! change %d\n"
fmt_back:   .string "returned %d\n"
fmt_reject: .string "rejected %d\n"
fmt_end:    .string "sold %d, holding %d\n"

.bss
.align 4
credit:     .skip 4                         // cents put in toward the next snack
sold:       .skip 4                         // snacks handed out so far
value_in:   .skip 4                         // scanf's landing spot

.text

// coin(w0 = coin value in cents, or 0 for the return lever)
        .balign 4
        .global coin
coin:
        // TODO: load the credit from .bss, decide what this input does,
        // print its one line, and store the new credit (and sold, after
        // a sale) back so the next call sees them.
        ret

        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp
        b       fill_test

next_value:
        ldr     x9, =value_in
        ldr     w0, [x9]
        bl      coin

fill_test:
        ldr     x0, =fmt_in
        ldr     x1, =value_in
        bl      scanf
        cmp     w0, 1                       // 1 value matched; -1 means the input ran out
        b.eq    next_value

        ldr     x0, =fmt_end
        ldr     x9, =sold
        ldr     w1, [x9]
        ldr     x9, =credit
        ldr     w2, [x9]
        bl      printf

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret

results.equals:

credit 35
credit 60
credit 70
vend! change 0
sold 1, holding 0
